evidence: Etymonline: "late 14c., cucomer, from Old French cocombre (13c...), from Latin cucumerem (nominative cucumis)... Replaced Old English eorþæppla (plural), literally 'earth-apples.' Cowcumber was the common form of the word in 17c.-18c.... Cucumber is an attempted reversion to Latin."
Wiktionary: "Displaced native earthapple, which has since acquired other senses."
cucumber.mechanism_sentence: cucumber 在拉丁语里就是黄瓜，一路没变：它换掉的是英语土生的『地苹果』(eorþæppla）——那是另一个词的故事。它自己只在读音上闹过笑话：两百年里英国人把它念作 cowcumber，『母牛瓜』。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
词义从未变过，变的是词形和读音：14世纪晚期它经法语以 cucomer 的样子进门，17—18世纪通行读法是 cowcumber；19世纪随着识字率上升，人们照拉丁拼法把读音『改回』了 cucumber。它顶替的古英语土词叫 eorþæppla『地苹果』，指的并不是它。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
